title: feat(plugin-security,platform-objects)!: a permission-set assignment shows its validity window and refuses an empty one (ADR-0091)
body:
Fixes #9272

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Time-bounded permission-set assignments on ADR-0091's grant-validity window. The maintainer's ruling, verbatim: 「9272 放到 v18开发」 — permission-set assignments only, ADR-0091's window vocabulary, no second time axis, enforce-with-declare. The declaration half was already on `main`: `sys_user_permission_set.valid_from` / `valid_until`, dropped outside the half-open window `[valid_from, valid_until)` at every resolution by `isGrantActive`. **This PR adds no field.** It adds:

1. **An end-to-end proof** that the window decides a user's real data access at every evaluation, with the grants cache on as well as off (H1). It holds on `main` unchanged.
2. **The authoring surface**: the user page's "Permission Sets" list shows the window; the window is set by editing the assignment row (H2).
3. **The derived refusal**: a write that leaves `valid_until` at or before `valid_from` is refused with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` (H3). **BREAKING**, graded `major` (Changesets pre mode, v18 line).

## H1 — enforcement, measured on `main`

All four behaviours hold on `origin/main` `54c3ce10` with no source change: the new dogfood pin's six enforcement cases were green there; its seventh case, the refusal, was red (`201`).

| Behaviour | Already pinned on `main` | New end-to-end pin: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/permission-set-assignment-window.dogfood.test.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| before `valid_from`: nothing | `core` `grant-validity.test.ts` "inactive before valid_from, active at and after it" (the predicate); `resolve-user-grants-cache.test.ts` pin 3 "the OTHER direction flips too: a future valid_from becomes active at its boundary" (a permission-set row, cache on, injected clock); `resolve-authz-context.test.ts` "a not-yet-active sys_user_position row (future valid_from) does not resolve" (position rows only: no uncached permission-set pin existed) | "an assignment before its valid_from grants nothing": `GET /data/showcase_invoice` answers 403 |
| inside the window: grants | `resolve-authz-context.test.ts` "a row inside its [from, until) window resolves; until is exclusive" (positions); the first leg of cache pin 3 (a permission-set row) | "an assignment inside [valid_from, valid_until) grants": 200 |
| at or after `valid_until`: nothing, at the next evaluation | `resolve-authz-context.test.ts` "an expired direct permission-set grant resolves to nothing — including platform_admin derivation" and "drops permission-set grants outside their validity window (ADR-0091)"; cache pin 3 "a grant whose valid_until falls inside the TTL stops resolving AT the boundary, not at TTL expiry" | "an assignment at or after its valid_until grants nothing": 403. "with the grants cache on, no cached answer outlives a window bound — with no write at the bound". "an administrator sets valid_until by editing the assignment row, and the next request is refused" |
| no window: unchanged (control) | `grant-validity.test.ts` "null/absent bounds = unbounded (pre-ADR-0091 rows unchanged)"; the unbounded `contributor` row in "an expired sys_user_position row does not resolve" | "an assignment with no window grants (the control)": 200, plus an armed precondition in `beforeAll` (a member with no grant reads 403, one with an unbounded grant 200) |

The pin boots the showcase with its own default profile (the CLI wiring). A plain member reads `showcase_invoice` only through a grant: `showcase_member_default` opens no read on it and `showcase_auditor` does (`examples/app-showcase/access-matrix.json`), so the door answers 200 exactly when the auditor assignment resolves. No existing dogfood pin did this: `delegation-of-duty.dogfood.test.ts` proves a delegated `sys_user_position` stops resolving at `valid_until` through `resolveAuthzContext`, not a permission-set assignment and not through a data door.

**The cache.** `resolveUserAuthzGrants` commits its cache entry with `nextGrantValidityBoundary(...)` over every row it applied the predicate to, inactive rows included (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:1160`), and the cache expires the entry at the earlier of its TTL and that bound (`resolve-user-grants-cache.ts:324`). Measured end to end on the real boot: with `OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` at one hour, one member's assignment ends and another's starts 6 s ahead; a second request before the bound issues no further read of the first member's grants (served from the cache — the pin asserts the read count), and the first request after the bound is refused for the one and served for the other, with no write anywhere at the bound.

**Precondition (#10982).** On `main` the organization-admin role projection honours the window: `resolve-authz-context.ts:856`-`860` filters `sys_member` rows with `isGrantActive` before the role derivation, pinned by `resolve-authz-context.test.ts` "#10982 — a lapsed sys_member row confers no role either".

## H2 — the authoring surface

- **Show the window: yes.** `record:related_list.columns` takes field names of `objectName` (`RecordRelatedListProps`, `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`), so the list now shows `valid_from` and `valid_until` beside the set. Pinned by `packages/platform-objects/src/pages/sys-user-permission-set-window-columns.test.ts` (red on `main`), which also parses the block through `RecordRelatedListProps`. No new label string: the columns carry the object's own field labels.
- **Set it at Add: no.** The `add` contract carries `picker`, `linkField` and `label` only, and the affordance writes exactly the two link keys. It cannot collect another field of the link row. Recorded below as a carrier note; nothing in `objectui` or `packages/spec` changes here.
- **Set it by editing the assignment row: yes.** `sys_user_permission_set` is `managedBy: 'system-data'`, whose CRUD affordances include `edit` (`resolveCrudAffordances`, pinned in `spec` `object.test.ts`), and both bounds are writable datetime fields. The dogfood pin drives what the record form submits, an administrator's `PATCH /data/sys_user_permission_set/:id` with `valid_until`, and the member's next request is refused. Not driven in a browser.

## H3 — the refusal

**Shape: a declared validation rule on the object** (`validity_window_order`, `cross_field`, in `objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts`), not a hook. Measured on `main`'s engine before writing it, on a scratch copy of the object carrying the rule (deleted after): the engine evaluates an object's declared rules on insert (single and batch) and on update (by id, and for each matched row of a multi-row update, which fetches the prior row for a `script` / `cross_field` rule), for system and non-system writers alike; the only context skip in the engine is the state-machine one. All 11 refusal pins below went green on that copy.

The rule refuses when both bounds are set and `datetime(valid_until)` is at or before `datetime(valid_from)` (equal bounds are an empty half-open window), and only on a write that makes the window: an insert (`previous == null`) or an update that moves a bound, judged on the stored row overlaid with the patch. An update that moves neither bound is not judged, so a row stored before this rule with an inverted window keeps taking unrelated edits. Stored inverted assignments in the showcase boot: **0** (asserted in the dogfood pin). The delegated-admin gate's own `valid_until` checks for delegated positions are untouched; the rule sits on `sys_user_permission_set` only.

Refused as `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with one field error, `rule_violation` at `valid_until`: read through `resolveThrownHttpError` at the engine, and from the response at the data door.

### The refusal pins: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/sys-user-permission-set-window-order.test.ts`

Real `ObjectQL` over a real SQL driver with the real `SecurityPlugin` started on it.

| Case | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| insert, inverted, system writer: refused, nothing stored | red | green |
| insert, inverted, administrator: refused, nothing stored | red | green |
| insert, equal bounds: refused | red | green |
| batch insert with one inverted row: refused whole | red | green |
| update by id moving `valid_until` before the stored `valid_from`: refused, stored row unchanged | red | green |
| update by id (system writer) moving `valid_from` onto the stored `valid_until`: refused, stored row unchanged | red | green |
| multi-row update inverting the matched windows: refused, no row moves | red | green |
| legacy inverted row: an unrelated update lands; moving one bound that leaves it inverted is refused; the repair lands | red (the refusal step) | green |
| control: a valid window lands | green | green |
| control: one bound alone (either) and no window land | green | green |
| control: moving a bound within a valid window lands | green | green |

### Ablation

Each mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed object file (blob `f64a027f`), restore proven each time (blob equals `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty, whole tree clean):

- **A1, the rule disabled** (`false && ` prefixed to the condition): 8 red — exactly the 8 that are red on `main`.
- **A2, the `previous` clause removed** (the rule becomes an invariant): 1 red — the legacy row's unrelated edit is refused. The clause is what keeps a stored violation from freezing the row.
- **A3, at-or-before weakened to strictly-before**: 2 red — the two equal-bound cases.
- **A1 through `dist/`, for the dogfood pin** (it resolves `@objectstack/plugin-security` through its built output): rebuilt; `ablation-dist-preflight` found the mutation's marker in 2 built files; the door case went red (`201`) and the six enforcement cases stayed green. Restore leg rebuilt: marker absent, the rule's name present in 4 built files, tree clean.

## Changesets and grade

- `@objectstack/plugin-security`: `major`, **BREAKING** banner, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — a refusal of one stored value combination on a data object; no metadata key, export or authorable surface moves.
- `@objectstack/platform-objects`: `minor` (the two list columns).
- The grade follows triage's release-state line (after #22080, a breaking change grades `major`; `.changeset/pre.json` is in `pre` mode on `main`). `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: "✓ Changesets is in pre-release mode (tag: next) — `major` bumps are the expected product of an RC window; skipping the no-major guard." Fed a pull-request payload carrying this body's declaration: "✓ LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `no (narrowing)`, and no package whose `packages/**/src/**` it moves is graded `patch`." `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`: "✓ check-adr-0087-registration: 1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition."
- The plugin-security translation bundles are regenerated with `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write --filter=security` for the rule's message; the translated locales carry the source text until translated, as the sibling rules' messages do.

## Tests, at `59875daf0a`

- `plugin-security`: full suite 187 files, 3895 passed, 45 skipped; `typecheck` exit 0 (test layer compiled, 0 errors).
- `platform-objects`: full suite 68 files, 1078 passed; `typecheck` exit 0.
- `dogfood`: the new pin 7 of 7; every dogfood file that writes or reads `sys_user_permission_set` (34 files) 34 passed, 358 tests passed, 1 skipped (on `main` with the pins: 33 of 34, the one red being the refusal); `typecheck` exit 0, the new file in the program (`--listFiles`).
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 69 commands (identical to the claim's reading), all run, all exit 0, reconciled by `--ran` ("69 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 69 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED"); `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first stopped at PREREQUISITE NOT MET (eight packages unbuilt in this worktree) and passed after building them. `pnpm check:error-status-conformance` by hand: "✓ every derivable runtime status is documented, and every documented status is reachable."
- ESLint, narrowed: the 12 changed TypeScript files, every one linted under `eslint.config.mjs` (none ignored), 0 errors, 0 warnings (`--no-inline-config --format json`). That config enables no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file; the repo-wide run is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Carrier note (not filed): Add-time collection of the window.** `record:related_list.add` (`RecordRelatedListProps`) writes the two link keys and collects nothing else, so a window cannot be set in the same step as the grant; it is set by editing the row. The missing capability is an `add` option that collects named fields of the link row before the insert — a contract key in `packages/spec` plus its renderer in `objectstack-ai/objectui`. Carrier: `objectstack-ai/objectui`.
- **The authz matrix row.** `authz-conformance.matrix.ts`'s `grant-validity-window` row names `delegation-of-duty.dogfood.test.ts` as its end-to-end proof. The new pin is a second, permission-set-shaped one; it carries no `authz-row:` claim, so the row and its pairing check are unchanged. Carrier: none.
- **A gate reading's wording.** `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` prints "direction arm: `narrowing` — a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships `minor`" while, in pre mode, it accepts the `major` this PR takes. The verdict and triage's line agree; only the arm line's sentence is stale in pre mode. Carrier: none.
- The window-order message is not translated in `zh-CN` / `ja-JP` / `es-ES` yet (source text, as above).
